tagline: Thirty-one miles of wildflower shoulders down to the Iowa line.
intro: From the interchange on I-90 east of Austin, Highway 56 runs due south to Rose Creek and then turns east for the Iowa line, 31 miles through farm country and small towns with old buildings of their own. It was one of Minnesota's first designated wildflower routes, and the state's highway and natural resources departments keep its roadsides in native grasses and flowers.
The name comes from the wildflowers that bloom along it in June and July.

moments.title: Taopi
moments.text: Named for the chief who befriended settlers after the New Ulm massacre, Taopi once had the largest steam-powered flour mill in southern Minnesota, good for 300,000 bushels of wheat a year.

moments.title: Lake Louise State Park
moments.text: The lake comes from an earthen dam on the Upper Iowa River, rebuilt by the people of Le Roy after the first one washed away and named for a settler's sister.

moments.title: Le Roy
moments.text: Platted in 1867 when the railroad got this far and named for a first settler's hometown in New York, Le Roy sits half a mile short of Iowa.
